about.title: Calabasas Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Calabasas may feel like a quieter corner of Los Angeles County, but its mix of office parks, retail centers, and construction along corridors near US-101 and Las Virgenes Road means workplace accidents still happen here. Whether you work in an office building off Calabasas Road, a job site near Mulholland Highway, or a retail space serving local residents, an on-the-job injury can leave you with medical bills and missed paychecks fast. In most cases, California workers' compensation is the path forward regardless of who caused the accident, but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, property owner, or piece of defective equipment played a role, a separate claim against that third party may be available alongside your workers' comp benefits. We review workplace injuries directly and can explain what options actually apply to your situation, free of charge.
about.ctaText: Contact us about your workplace injury — free and no obligation.

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Only Option
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the usual exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment manufacturer — can still be pursued separately. We can help sort out which path or paths apply to your case.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter
items.desc: California law generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days to preserve your workers' comp rights. Missing that window can complicate things, so getting guidance early matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Against the Law
items.desc: Employers cannot legally punish a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about your job because you got hurt, we can explain your protections.

items.question: I got hurt at a Calabasas job site — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: In most situations, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, meaning a lawsuit against them typically isn't an option. However, if someone other than your employer — like a subcontractor or property owner along Calabasas Road or a nearby site — contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may be possible. We can review the facts and tell you which routes apply.

items.question: How long do I have to act after a workplace injury in Calabasas?
items.answer: You generally need to notify your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' comp rights. If a third-party claim is involved, California law generally allows two years from the date of injury to file that separate claim. Waiting too long can limit your options, so it's worth getting information sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if my employer retaliates after I report an injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. If you believe you've faced pushback, demotion, or termination connected to your injury report, we can review what happened and explain your rights.
